overview: The MPS Meeting of the Whole serves as a forum for the full School Committee to conduct in-depth policy development, budget planning, and administrative oversight. The body is responsible for reconciling school operating costs with municipal allocations, updating district-wide policies, and managing the annual performance review of the Superintendent. Having met from 2020 through 2026, the committee has overseen major transitions in school naming and internal governance rules. Most recently, the body is focused on addressing significant projected budget deficits and monitoring the multi-year design process for the high school construction project.

threads.name: Superintendent Performance Evaluation
threads.summary: The body manages the annual evaluation of Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent, establishing focus indicators and review timelines. Early sessions centered on 2019-2020 performance metrics and the creation of formal evaluation procedures by subcommittee. Later, the committee established a standing Evaluation Subcommittee and shifted to using state rubric indicators such as instructional leadership and cultural proficiency. The process involves receiving self-evaluations and approving composite committee ratings, which most recently resulted in a proficient summative performance rating.

threads.name: Fiscal Planning and Budget Reconciliation
threads.summary: The committee conducts extensive reviews of annual budget requests, frequently addressing gaps between projected district needs and municipal allocations. Discussions often focus on the impact of expiring federal ESSER relief funds, leading to warnings of a fiscal funding cliff for personnel and technology. Finance staff provide regular updates on Chapter 70 state aid, revenue collection audits, and the use of revolving accounts to offset operational costs. Recent meetings have addressed a $5 million gap in the preliminary fiscal year 2027 budget and the necessity of potential staffing reductions.

threads.name: Governance and Internal Rules
threads.summary: In early 2022, the body undertook a comprehensive revision of its internal operating rules and standing subcommittee structures. Key updates included changing meeting start times, establishing adjournment deadlines, and refining agenda-setting protocols between the Chair and Superintendent. The committee also restructured subcommittees to ensure they only conduct business referred by a majority vote of the full body. The process concluded with the adoption of a finalized rules document that standardized communication protocols with the City Council and public participation rules.

threads.name: Columbus Elementary School Renaming
threads.summary: The committee established the formal process for renaming Columbus Elementary School, including the structure and selection mechanics for a 23-member advisory committee. Members defined application criteria, prohibited specific names from consideration, and coordinated with district policy to ensure diverse stakeholder representation. The body finalized the renaming resolution and selected voting members through a combination of appointments and a random lottery. The process included mandates for open meeting requirements and a specific reporting timeline for name recommendations.

threads.name: Facility Modernization and MSBA Projects
threads.summary: Initial work involved relaunching the Medford High School Vision Committee to address long-term educational and facility needs, with an emphasis on carbon neutrality. The body manages capital improvement priorities, such as HVAC stabilization and laboratory renovations. More recently, the committee authorized the submission of Statements of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority for elementary school roof and heat pump repairs. The building committee provides ongoing updates on the high school construction project, including the selection of design options and grant applications.

threads.name: School Climate and Equity Policy
threads.summary: The body reviews and amends district policies to align with state regulations, including the adoption of non-discrimination policies regarding gender identity. Following safety incidents at the high school, the committee commissioned and reviewed an external consultant's report that recommended administrative restructuring and unified leadership committees. The committee continues to monitor school-wide behavioral norms and receives reports on student wellness, including survey data on cafeteria overcrowding and transportation services.
